gp.heading: Gross Margins
gp.text:
In 2024, Nucor recorded gross margins of $4.10 billion (13%), which was a decrease from $7.82 billion (23%) in 2023:

The primary driver for the decrease in gross margins in 2024 as compared to 2023 was the decrease in gross margins in the steel products segment. Gross margins decreased across most businesses within the segment due to lower volumes and decreased average selling prices. The largest decreases were at our joist and deck businesses, as average selling prices and volumes continued to moderate from the historically high levels reached in 2022.

Gross margins in the steel mills segment decreased 2024 compared to 2023 due to decreased metal margins. The average scrap and scrap substitute cost per gross ton used decreased 6% from $421 in 2023 to $394 in 2024. Despite the decrease in average scrap and scrap substitute costs in 2024 compared to 2023, metal margins decreased as the decrease in average selling prices was greater than the decrease in average scrap and scrap substitute costs. Scrap prices are driven by the global supply and demand for scrap and other iron-based raw materials used to make steel. Scrap prices are stable as we begin 2025.

Pre-operating and start-up costs of new facilities increased to approximately $594 million in 2024 as compared to approximately $400 million in 2023.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The steel mills segment is Nucor’s largest segment, representing 62% of the Company’s sales to external customers in the year ended December 31, 2025.
We estimate that approximately 85% of our sheet steel sales in 2025 were to contract customers.
Our largest single customer in 2025 represented approximately 5% of sales and consistently pays within terms.
Approximately 85% of our sheet sales were to contract customers in 2025, with the balance being sold in the spot market at the prevailing prices at the time of sale.
The Company’s operations include international trading and sales companies that buy and sell steel and steel products manufactured by the Company and others.

The steel mills segment also includes Nucor’s equity method investment in NuMit LLC (“NuMit”) (see “Steel joint venture”- below), as well as international trading and distribution companies that buy and sell steel manufactured by the Company and other steel producers.

The number of tons sold to contract customers at any given time depends on a variety of factors, including our consideration of current and future market conditions, our strategy to appropriately balance spot and contract tons in a manner to meet our customers’ requirements while considering the expected profitability, our desire to sustain a diversified customer base, and our end-use customers’ perceptions about future market conditions.
Electra’s technology relies on intermittent electrical energy to refine low-grade iron ores through electrochemical and hydrometallurgical processes.
We rely upon third parties for our supply of energy resources consumed in the manufacture of our products.

The amount of tons sold to contract customers at any given time depends on the overall market conditions at the time, how the end-use customers see the market moving forward and the strategy that Nucor management believes is appropriate to the upcoming period.
The percentage of tons that is placed under contract also depends on the overall market dynamics and customer negotiations.
The timing and amount of repurchases, if any, depend on market conditions, share price, applicable legal requirements and other factors.
Nucor disaggregates its revenues by major source in the same manner as presented in the net sales by product table in the segment footnote (see Note 22).
